doc.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025

title: Quitting the day job and odd jobs in Evanston
summary: Levy explains he left jobs like waterbed frames, plumber's assistant and furniture moving to commit to music, teaching harmonica and piano.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Was there a circumstance or a series of months that helped you decide that you could quit your day job?

Oh yeah. When I couldn’t stand dragging myself to work. One day it was like I just can’t do this anymore. I can’t get on the L in these work clothes and go and make waterbed frames anymore. I can’t do it.

Yeah, yeah. Oh man, I was a plumber’s assistant, I was a furniture mover, a house painter, I mean I did all this stuff. But the whole time of course I was working on my music and expanding my musical vocabulary and studying a lot of stuff, and teaching too. I was teaching harmonica and piano. And then at a certain point I just realized I cannot, I cannot do these two things at once. I have to just take the plunge, take a risk, and of course life was more affordable back then, and rent wasn’t, you know you didn’t have to pay an arm and a leg to rent an apartment in Evanston back in the ‘70s, and so I let go of all that stuff and plunged into it and, you know, I have to say Chicago was a very good place for me to do that.
